questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers NOT be kept?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
Within reach of the driver while wearing the seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's side door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be quick to reach in an emergency. Keep papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view within arm's reach while your seat belt is fastened. You can keep papers on the driver's seat when you leave the vehicle.

questions.question: Who decides what hazard class a shipped material belongs to?
questions.explanation: The shipper identifies the hazard class, product ID number, shipping name, packing group, and ensures correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.

questions.question: What is a Class 7 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 7 hazardous materials are radioactive materials.

questions.question: What should you do when a construction worker is near the road ahead?

options.text: Wait until construction ends before driving.

questions.explanation: When driving through work zones with workers near the road, reduce your speed.

questions.question: What should a driver always do?
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead to spot hazards early. Plan how you will handle each hazard if it becomes dangerous.

questions.question: Which exhaust system condition does NOT need attention?

options.text: Exhaust system parts not rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts not rubbing against fuel system parts
questions.explanation: Check for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, or brackets. Look for parts rubbing against fuel system parts or tires. Check for leaks. Parts that are NOT rubbing or leaking are fine.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand brake during a jackknife?
questions.explanation: Release the brakes during a jackknife to help your tires regain grip. Using the trailer hand brake will only make the skid continue.

questions.question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?

options.text: Move forward slowly and use the brake pedal.
Reverse slowly and use the hand control.
Reverse slowly and use the brake pedal.
Move forward slowly and use the hand control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly and use the hand control.
questions.explanation: First check that air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and use the hand control to apply the brakes. If working properly, you will feel the brakes engage.

questions.question: What should you do if you might be late to your destination?

options.text: Use flashing lights to make others move.
Drive safely and arrive when you arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Avoid unsafe and aggressive driving. Accept delays and relax. Plan extra time when scheduling a trip to avoid stress about being late.

questions.question: What condition should engine belts be in?
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and excessive wear. Each belt's acceptable amount of movement varies by vehicle, so learn what is correct for your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all brakes. Listen for air escaping. Then close both shut-off valves before you drive.

questions.question: What should you do if cargo is leaking?

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify what it is.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Spray the leaking containers with water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: If you find a leak in hazardous materials, use the shipping papers and labels to identify what is leaking. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: A maximum of two inches of space

questions.explanation: Before a trip, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: When are most drivers the least alert?
questions.explanation: Fatigue and lack of alertness are major hazards at night. Most people are least alert at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire fails?
questions.explanation: Using brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Stay off the brakes, if possible, until your vehicle slows down.

questions.question: What indicates that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Packaging can show whether materials are hazardous. Cylinders and drums are often used to hold and transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: Is eating while driving safe?

options.text: Yes, it is a good way to save time.
No, it is a dangerous activity.
Yes, if the food is easy to eat.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is a dangerous activity.
questions.explanation: Smoking, eating, and drinking are distracting and should be avoided while driving. Plan ahead and take time to stop and eat on long trips.

questions.question: Many products classed as poison are also:
questions.explanation: Many products classed as poison are also flammable. Take the right precautions if you think your cargo may be flammable.

questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot move in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is difficult to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Avoid backing whenever possible.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, what should you avoid?

options.text: Canceling the turn signal after completing the turn.
Leaving the turn signal on long after the turn is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leaving the turn signal on long after the turn is completed.
questions.explanation: Signal early before turning or changing lanes. Keep the signal on until you complete the turn or lane change. Then turn off the signal so other drivers are not confused.
